messages:
morgan_ops: Heads up — saw an ECC spike across eu-west pool8 between 03:10–03:30 UTC, card-level correctables up ~8x vs baseline. Some pods got soft OOM retries.

 taylor_infra: That sounds bad. Is it concentrated on one host or spread?

 morgan_ops: Spread across 6 different hosts but all in the same rack. Pattern looks like short bursts lasting ~30–90s.

 devon_sre: Can you paste the metric query you used?

 morgan_ops: sure — `sum(rate(gpu_ecc_correctable_total[2m])) by (card, instance)` then filtered for > 0.02/s. Example output pinned as CSV in #ops-logs.

 sasha_repair: Quick thought — could be a firmware regression after last night's rolling maintenance. Any matching firmware version on those cards?

 morgan_ops: I checked — 4 hosts had FW vR2.1.8, 2 had vR2.1.6. Doesn't map cleanly.

 devon_sre: Suggest we avoid global auto-evac until we confirm noisy-card count and impact on capacity. Propose: 1) Enrich signal with consecutive-window rule, 2) Temporarily bias routing away from affected rack, 3) If a card exceeds 3x baseline for 10m, mark for quarantine.

 taylor_infra: Agreed on enrichment. What about threshold calc? We used static rate before which triggers too often on bursty IO loads.

 devon_sre: New formula idea: threshold = max(absolute_min, baseline_95p + k * baseline_std) where k=2.5 for production pools, but we also require monotonicity (must exceed for N windows).

 sasha_repair: Also include Y = number of distinct jobs impacted on that host; if Y>2 then escalate to replacement queue earlier.

 morgan_ops: Ops-bot alerted about a training job failing with repeated CUDA XID 31 around same time. Linking error dump.

 ops-bot: Incident created: #INC-2024-3409. Assigned to devon_sre.

 devon_sre: For immediate mitigation I pushed a soft-reroute rule to avoid pool8 rack for 15m, and disabled aggressive auto-drain for the rack while we investigate. Patch: `routing.set_bias(rack=pool8, weight=0.2, ttl=900)`

 taylor_infra: Can you also run a dry-run of the quarantine logic to see how many cards would have been flagged in the last 48h?

 devon_sre: Running now: `python infra/tools/quarantine_sim.py --lookback 48h --window 2m --mult 2.5` — result: 7 cards flagged across last 48h, but only 2 would have met the 10m sustained rule.

 sasha_repair: Ok so we avoid panic replacement. Next steps: schedule targeted repro on those 2 cards during repair window, capture ECC dump and nvme/power telemetry, and if repro fails, plan hot-swap next maintenance window.

 morgan_ops: Also we should tweak alerting to include job-impacted metric so noisy-but-harmless spikes don't trigger page. Add runbook pointer to static threshold doc.

 taylor_infra: I updated the alert query to require a second signal: `gpu_job_error_rate > 0.5%` OR `gpu_ecc_correctable_total sustained > threshold for 10m`. Lower false positives.

 devon_sre: Good. I'll open a short RFC for changing auto-drain to conservative mode during regional maintenance windows and for rack-local quarantines (instead of pool-wide).

 sasha_repair: Booking repro window 2024-11-12 02:00–04:00 UTC. I'll bring spare cards and test harness.

 morgan_ops: Thanks team. Leaving the soft-reroute in place for 30m. Will post updates to #oncall when we have dumps. :thumbsup:

 devon_sre: Follow-ups: 1) telemetry enrichment (add power rails, pci-e errors) 2) RFC for new threshold formula 3) repair doc update. I'll track in INC 2024-3409.

 ops-bot: INC-2024-3409 status changed to investigating.

 morgan_ops: End of thread — will reopen if new spikes show up.
